title: A 'gym closed today' notice sent as the third message of the day reaches no member's phone as a pop-up
what: From the third gym message of an India day, the server marks every message quiet: it shows in the app's list but no phone pops up. The count makes no exception for urgent kinds such as 'gym closed' or a timing change, and it also counts the automatic messages the server writes itself, such as the challenge winners' message. So an owner who already sent two messages, or whose challenge just ended, can send 'Gym closed today' and nobody's phone rings. Member apps older than the first release after 0.60.0 do the opposite and still pop the quiet message up.
expected: An urgent notice (gym closed, timing change) always pops up, and automatic messages the owner did not write do not use up the owner's two pop-ups a day.
how_often: any day with two or more messages before an urgent one
fix_line: Never make 'closed' and 'timing' messages quiet, and leave automatic messages out of the day's count.

title: The server never records how many phones a gym message's pop-up reached, and logs one that reached no phone as sent
what: A gym message's 'sent to' number counts every app member of the gym, whether or not their phone can show a pop-up. When the pop-up goes out, the server keeps only a running count and, when no phone at all had a push address, it closes the job as 'sent'. The newer personal pop-ups say 'no phone' in the same case, but gym messages, offers and trainer replies do not. So neither the owner nor MettleUp can tell how many members a message really rang, or who will never get one.
expected: Each message keeps how many members' phones were reached, a job with no phone says 'no phone', and the owner can see that number next to 'sent to'.
how_often: every gym message, offer and trainer reply
fix_line: Record phones reached per message, mark no-phone jobs as such, and show the reached count to the owner.

title: Asking a member for their workout report can reach nobody, and the desk is only told it is waiting
what: The desk can ask any member on the gym's list for their workout report. The member's phone only gets the pop-up, and the app only shows the request, when that member's number was proven at the door, no one else on the list has the same number, and the first name matches. Otherwise the request just waits until it runs out. The desk's answer shows the request as waiting, with no sign that no app will ever see it.
expected: When asking, the desk is told if the member cannot get the request in the app (no app, number not proven, shared number or name differs) and why.
how_often: every report request to a member without a matched app
fix_line: Check the app match when the report is asked for and tell the desk if no app can see it.

title: An owner whose MettleUp payment is rejected or confirmed is not told
what: When MettleUp HQ confirms or rejects the reference number an owner sent for their plan payment, the server only changes the payment's state and writes the reason. No message, bell or pop-up goes to the owner; they learn it only by opening the Pay MettleUp page again. An owner who thinks they paid can slide into the grace and limited states without knowing the payment was turned down. This part is not switched on live yet.
expected: The owner gets a bell message (and a pop-up if alerts are on) when their payment is confirmed or rejected, with the reason.
how_often: every rejected or confirmed payment once switched on
fix_line: Send the owner a bell message when HQ confirms or rejects a payment.
